title: Networking and Time
summary: Rust in Action's networking and time chapters: the layers of the network stack, HTTP spoken by hand over TCP, ports, DNS and UDP; error types that wrap other errors, MAC addresses and protocol state machines as enums; and how computers keep time, from Unix and NTP timestamps to monotonic clocks and clock synchronization.
goals: Explain the network layers and write raw HTTP requests over std::net::TcpStream to a local server
Resolve names to socket addresses and send UDP datagrams
Define a library error type that wraps io, parse and address errors with From and ?
Model MAC addresses and a TCP-like connection as Rust types
Use SystemTime, Instant and Duration, format timestamps as RFC 3339, and compute NTP offset and delay
